survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This note reports results from the OECD Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2024 for lower secondary teachers and principals in Alberta (Canada). The document does not provide the underlying microdata weighting variables or replicate-weight methodology, but TALIS estimates are produced from a complex survey design and are typically computed using sampling weights to account for unequal selection probabilities and non-response. The note also flags that Alberta (Canada) did not meet TALIS participation rate standards, implying higher risk of non-response bias and therefore reduced confidence in the precision of estimates. Analysts using the TALIS 2024 database should apply the official TALIS sampling weights and follow the TALIS technical documentation for variance estimation; this note itself is descriptive and does not specify weight variable names.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive policy note based on TALIS self-reports (percentages and agreement/stress/working-time indicators) rather than cognitive achievement scores with plausible values. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported outcomes. Missing-data handling is not reported because the note does not present an analytic modeling pipeline (e.g., imputation/deletion rules) and instead summarizes OECD-produced TALIS estimates from the TALIS database tables.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TALIS 2024 responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals in Alberta (Canada). The note does not specify additional analytic exclusions (e.g., item non-response rules) and only states that Alberta is annotated because it did not meet TALIS participation rate standards, implying caution due to higher non-response bias.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 note summarizes descriptive results for Alberta (Canada) using self-reported questionnaire data from lower secondary teachers and principals collected in 2024. The note reports percentages and agreement levels across multiple policy-relevant domains (teachers’ background, teaching for today’s world, student diversity, special needs, social and emotional skills, technology/AI use, learning opportunities, induction/mentoring, professional relationships, status of the profession, employment terms, demands of teaching, classroom management, appraisal, and professional outcomes). It only comments on statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average and flags Alberta as annotated because it did not meet TALIS participation rate standards, increasing the risk of non-response bias. No student-level predictive modeling or plausible-value scaling is presented; therefore, the document functions as an evidence summary for policy discussion rather than an ML-based causal or predictive analysis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical ML/predictive paper: it is a descriptive OECD results note based on TALIS 2024 database tables. Consequently, there is no reported student-level analytic sample size, no ML algorithms, no plausible-value generation/combining, and no model-based performance metrics to extract. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and focuses on the survey-based descriptive comparisons and the participation-rate caution.
